P0313.d: When the tank is nearly empty the fuel pump can draw air in corners or on gradients, which causes misfires. CARB allows misfire detection to be switched off at 15 % fuel or less; some manufacturers instead report misfires detected in this state under P0313 rather than P030x.
s: Check engine light on (flashing at a catalyst-damaging rate)
Jerking or power loss with an almost empty tank, especially in corners or uphill
c: Tank nearly empty – the fuel pump draws air (corners, gradients, braking)
Actual misfire cause (ignition, injector, false air) that happened at low fuel
Weak fuel pump, clogged strainer or filter, faulty swirl pot
Fuel level sender reading too low

P0314.d: P0314 means the misfire is attributable to a single cylinder, but the module does not say which one. CARB generally requires cylinder-specific codes and allows a general code only with approval where the cylinder cannot be identified reliably; for diesels identification is required only where possible without extra hardware.
s: Loss of power, limp mode with quantity limit (Saab diesel)
c: Injector of one cylinder clogged or leaking (diesel), or coil/plug (petrol)
Leaking high-pressure line, fuel bridge or injector washer
Air, water or petrol in the diesel, clogged filter, low supply pressure

P0315.d: Manufacturing tolerances of the crankshaft tone wheel distort the speed fluctuations misfire detection relies on, so the engine module learns a correction for each tooth or segment. P0315 means these values have not been learned or are invalid.
s: Check engine light on (GM; Ford depending on application)
Misfire readiness not set – emissions test fails
c: Relearn not performed after replacing sensor, crankshaft, damper, engine or engine module
Learned values lost through voltage loss (battery disconnected)
Tone wheel damaged or shifted, crankshaft runout, dirt on the sensor
Interference in the crankshaft sensor circuit

P0316.d: P0316 concerns misfire within the first 1,000 revolutions after start. CARB requires a pending code here after the first exceedance of the emissions-relevant rate (later in the drive only after the fourth) and the warning light if it recurs at the next start.
s: Rough running right after a cold start, then normal
Delayed start, fuel smell at start
c: Moisture or water in the plug wells, coils arcing when cold or damp
Leaking injectors (fuel drips after switch-off, over-rich start)
Worn or sooted spark plugs that only fire cleanly when warm
Wrong temperature sensor value or engine software

ABS/ESP module not responding (supply, CAN line)

Ford checks continuously from 200–500 rpm and sets it within 5 s when the number of teeth after the gap is wrong, the tooth time is implausible (below 30 or above 9,000 rpm) or the gap appears in the
s: Reduced power on electronic throttle (Ford P2106)

P0321.d: P0321 belongs to the same signal as P0320 and P0322: the speed and reference input of the ignition, formerly the distributor's Hall pickup, today practically always the crankshaft position sensor. Range/Performance means a signal is present but implausible – wrong number of teeth between the reference gaps, erratic tooth times, or a speed that does not fit the camshaft signal.
c: Crankshaft position sensor faulty or aged (weak, noisy signal)
Sensor loose or air gap wrong
Tone wheel damaged or clogged with metal chips
Interference, poor ground or damaged wiring

P0322.d: P0322 means the speed and reference input of the ignition – today the crankshaft position sensor – delivers no signal although the engine is turning. Ford proves the rotation with the camshaft sensor: if it shows more than one engine revolution without a crank signal (from 500 rpm, detected within 5 s), Ford sets P0322 or, depending on the engine, P0335; with electronic throttle the throttle software adds P2106 and g
s: Engine cranks but does not start
Check engine light on, with electronic throttle limp mode (P2106)
c: Open or short in signal, ground or 5 V supply, corroded connector
Sensor loose, air gap too large or tone wheel damaged
5 V reference pulled down by another sensor on the same supply

P0323.d: P0323 stands for a speed and reference signal at the ignition input – today the crankshaft position sensor – that drops out or is disturbed for moments and then recovers. None of the manufacturer documents available to us (GM 2014–2019, Ford 2012 and 2020–2023, Saab workshop information) uses P0323; the sporadic crank sensor check runs under P0339 at Ford and under P0336 at GM.
s: Brief stumbling or stalling, then normal again
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector

P0324.d: P0324 concerns the knock control as a whole rather than a single sensor circuit. Audible pinging or knocking under load
c: Genuine knock: low-octane fuel, carbon deposits, high intake or coolant temperature, lean mixture
Mechanical noise taken for knock (loose parts, brackets, valve train, bearings)
Knock sensor damaged, wrongly torqued or mounted with sealant

GM sets it after at least 4 resynchronisations in under 5 s, a gap not found within 0.4 s running or 1.5 s cranking, or a wrong tooth count in 8 of 10 revolutions,

c: Tone wheel damaged, bent, loose or teeth clogged with chips
Sensor signal weak or noisy (air gap, ageing)
Wrong tone wheel or flywheel fitted after a repair

P0337.d: By its J2012 name P0337 means the crankshaft position signal stays at a low level without changing state – signal wire shorted to ground, missing supply on a Hall sensor or a sensor stuck low. Few manufacturers use the code.

Engine stalls while driving or at idle
Tachometer drops to zero or flickers
c: Signal wire shorted to ground or open
Crankshaft position sensor faulty (output stuck low)
Connector corroded or pin pushed back

P0338.d: By its J2012 name P0338 means the crankshaft position signal stays at a high level – signal wire shorted to supply, or an open signal output that the module's pull-up holds high on a Hall sensor. GM 2014–2019 and Ford do not use the code.
c: Signal wire shorted to supply or open (pull-up holds the level high)
Interference pulses from poor ground or shielding
Tone wheel damaged or dirty (gap not recognised)

P0339.d: P0339 means the crankshaft position signal drops out or is disturbed for moments and then recovers. Ford's 2020–2023 petrol engines use it, depending on the engine, instead of P0320 for tooth errors: wrong tooth count after the gap, tooth time outside 30 to 9,000 rpm, gap at an unexpected position, from 500 rpm, detected within 5 s.
s: Check engine light on (not on all Ford engines)
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector or an in-line connector
Sensor mounting or air gap mechanically wrong (machining error, bracket)

Timing chain or belt jumped or heavily stretched

P0340.d: The camshaft position sensor, almost always a Hall sensor, tells the engine module which stroke cylinder 1 is in – one crank revolution alone is ambiguous – and measures the actual cam phase with variable timing. Sensor A is the intake camshaft, bank 1 the side with cylinder 1.

Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)
c: Connector or wiring corroded or open, 5 V reference disturbed
Tone wheel on the camshaft or phaser damaged, loose or at the wrong distance
Timing drive jumped or wrongly assembled
Moisture in the engine oil from short trips (Ford hybrids)

P0341.d: P0341 means the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) delivers pulses, but their number or pattern does not fit the crankshaft. GM counts the pulses while the crank is in sync: 4 to 6 in the first 12 reference events and 398 to 402 per 100 engine cycles on the 4X wheel of the cam phaser; outside that in 8 of 10 checks the code is set after two trips.
s: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)
c: Sensor with interference pulses or weak signal, air gap
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or wrongly fitted

P0342.d: P0342 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) stays at ground level without edges – signal wire shorted to ground, sensor supply missing or the Hall sensor faulty. Ford's 2023 diesel sets it when the signal stays at 0 V over 10 or more crank revolutions (3 s), while cranking or running.
s: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)
c: 5 V or 12 V supply of the sensor missing

P0343.d: P0343 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) stays at supply level without edges. Causes are a signal wire shorted to positive, an open signal wire that the module's pull-up holds at 5 V, a broken sensor ground or a faulty sensor.
s: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)
c: Signal wire open or shorted to positive

P0344.d: P0344 means the signal of the intake camshaft sensor of bank 1 (or the only cam sensor) is disturbed for moments: edges are missing or appear at an unexpected angle. Ford checks this on the five-tooth wheel used with variable cam timing; if edges appear where none are expected, Ford sets P0344 and switches cam timing off (loss of power and torque), from 200 rpm, detected within 5 s.
s: Sporadic loss of power (cam timing off)
c: Moisture or oil inside the sensor, dropping out when hot
Loose contact or corrosion at the connector
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or loose

s: Longer cranking before the engine starts
Loss of power (cam timing held in its base position)

Tone wheel or phaser of bank 2 damaged

P034A.d: Engines with start-stop or hybrid autostart store the crankshaft rest position when the engine stops, so that they can inject and fire correctly at once on restart. P037A.d: Diesel engines show the driver a wait-to-start lamp while the glow plugs preheat; the engine module switches it with a high-side driver. P037A means the lamp control circuit is too low – in practice a short to ground on the line to the instrument cluster.
s: Glow plug light does not come on or stays dim
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early, possibly poor cold start
c: Lamp control wire chafed through to ground between engine module and cluster
Lamp or LED driver in the instrument cluster shorted internally
Moisture or corrosion in the module or cluster connector
Driver in the engine module faulty

P037B.d: P037B is the counterpart of P037A: the control circuit of the wait-to-start lamp is too high, i.e. the line carries voltage although the engine module's driver is off, or the driver sees a short to battery voltage.
s: Glow plug light stays on or flickers
Check engine light on (after two trips)
c: Lamp control wire chafed against battery or ignition positive
Fault in the instrument cluster feeding voltage back
Water damage in a connector bridging to a neighbouring pin
Driver in the engine module faulty

P037C.d: To heat the catalyst quickly after a cold start, some engines select a particular camshaft profile; CARB counts altered valve timing among these cold-start measures and requires components of the cold-start strategy to have their own diagnostics. P037C checks whether the requested profile is actually engaged during this phase.
s: Rough running or stalling when cold (for example on remote start)
c: Profile actuator (sliding cam pin) sticking or not switching
Wrong oil viscosity or low oil level, mechanism stiff when cold

P037D.d: To check the glow plugs, the engine module reads back the voltage or current of the glow plug supply through a sense circuit – CARB requires glow plug circuits to be monitored for correct current and voltage drop, and from model year 2010 the failure of a single plug to be detected. In the J2012 scheme P037D is the general code for this sense circuit, P037E and P037F its low and high counterparts.
s: Check engine light or glow plug light on
Possibly poor cold start if the cause also affects the glow plug supply
c: Sense wire open or high resistance, connector corroded
Glow relay or glow plug control module giving an implausible feedback
Fuse or fusible link of the glow plug supply blown

P037E.d: P037E means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too low. GM's 2016/2018 diesels, whose glow plug output stages sit in the engine module, compare the feedback with the battery voltage while glowing: if it is lower by more than a calibrated, current-dependent threshold – excessive voltage drop or a short to ground of the sense line – a sample counts as faulty, and 60 of 120 samples in a 50 ms grid set th
s: Possibly hard starting or knocking when cold
c: High contact resistance in the glow plug supply (connector, ground, fusible link)
Measuring circuit or output stage in the engine module
Sense or supply wire shorted to ground
Weak battery or vehicle voltage at the edge of the enable range

P037F.d: P037F means the voltage read back from the glow plug supply is too high. GM's 2016/2018 diesels set it when the feedback lies above a threshold derived from the run/crank relay voltage, with a feedback above 5.0 V – for example voltage is reported although the plugs are not energised, or the sense line is shorted to positive.
s: Glow plugs possibly energised permanently (flat battery, plug damage)
c: Sense wire chafed against positive or bridged in the connector
Glow relay sticking or output stage shorted (supply stays on)
Measuring circuit in the engine module

P0380.d: P0380 concerns glow plug circuit A – depending on the manufacturer the first group of plugs, glow relay 1 or feedback line A of the glow plug control module. Saab's 3.0 TiD (9-5, 2002) has two feedback lines from the control module; if line A at the engine module stays above 4.0 V for more than 3 s while glowing, the module is reporting a plug or circuit fault, checked once per drive cycle with the warning lamp on.
s: Hard starting when cold, long cranking
White or blue smoke and rough running after a cold start
Glow plug light or check engine light on or flashing
c: Glow plug(s) in circuit A burnt out
Glow plug control module or glow relay faulty
Wiring or connector fault (feedback line, plug connector, supply)
Missing battery or ignition supply of the control module (fuse)

P0381.d: P0381 monitors the circuit of the wait-to-start lamp for an open circuit or, more generally, for faults that keep the lamp dark when commanded – CARB names a burnt-out bulb as the example, with exemptions for LCD clusters and for engines that only release the starter after preheating. GM's 2015–2018 diesels detect an open circuit in the driver by a high load impedance (about 200 kΩ in 2015), in 0.2 s or 10 of 15 samp
s: Glow plug light does not come on at key-on
Check engine light on (GM after two trips)
Driver starts too early in the cold
c: Control wire open or connector fault between engine module and cluster
Lamp or LED in the instrument cluster burnt out
Instrument cluster faulty or communication problem (Ford)

s: Hard starting when cold, long cranking

P0383.d: Many diesels have a separate glow plug control module that the engine module commands over a control line. P0383 means this line is too low.
s: Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer
c: Control line between engine module and glow plug module shorted to ground or open
Corroded connector at the glow plug module in the engine bay
Glow plug control module faulty (input pulls the line down)

P0384.d: P0384 is the counterpart of P0383: the control line from the engine module to the glow plug control module is too high, i.e. shorted to positive.
s: No or irregular preheating, hard starting when cold
Warning lamp depending on the manufacturer
c: Control line chafed against positive or bridged in the connector
Glow plug control module faulty internally (feeding back)
Ford: supply of the module outside 6.5–16.5 V or open (battery, alternator, fuse)

P0385.d: Some engines have a second crankshaft sensor or a second track on the tone wheel, which the engine module checks against sensor A or the camshaft. P0385 means its signal is missing or does not match.
c: Connector or wiring open or corroded
Tone wheel or second track damaged

P0386.d: P0386 means the signal of the second crankshaft sensor or second tone wheel track is present but implausible. GM's 2004 Northstar 4.6 V8 sets it after 5 resynchronisations within 10 s, after two trips.
c: Interference pulses (wiring near the ignition, shielding)
Sensor dirty or air gap wrong

s: Rough running, no start if sensor A also fails

P0390.d: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0390 means no or too few exhaust cam pulses arrive from bank 2 while the crankshaft turns.
s: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)
c: Connector or wiring of the bank 2 exhaust sensor open or corroded (signal, 5 V, ground)
Oil contamination or leak at the sensor, sensor loose
Tone wheel on the phaser damaged or wrongly fitted after timing chain work
Engine module, or 5 V reference shorted by another sensor

P0391.d: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0391 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal is present, but the number or position of its pulses does not fit the crankshaft.
s: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)
c: Tone wheel on the bank 2 exhaust phaser damaged, loose or wrongly fitted
Interference or loose contact producing extra edges
Sensor loose, wrong O-ring or gap, chips on the magnet

P0392.d: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0392 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal stays low without edges – typically a short to ground of the signal wire, a sensor output stuck low or a missing 5 V reference.
s: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)
c: 5 V reference missing (shorted by another sensor on the same circuit)

P0393.d: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0393 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal stays high without edges.
s: Loss of power (bank 2 exhaust cam timing in its base position)
c: Signal wire open or connector off

P0394.d: Camshaft position sensor B is the exhaust camshaft sensor; bank 2 is the side without cylinder 1, so the code only occurs on V and boxer engines with one exhaust cam sensor per bank. P0394 means the bank 2 exhaust cam signal now and then appears at a position where it is not expected relative to the crank reference – sporadic extra or missing edges.
c: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector or harness
Interference (ignition wiring, add-on devices, ground problems)
Tone wheel or phaser damaged, or sensor loose

The code concerns this logic-level signal, not the coil's primary circuit (coil K has its own codes, P0361 and P2330 ff).
